app.title: Countess
app.summary: The person chooses a folder of microscope slide images. The app works through the images one at a time in name order. For each image it finds the slide's counting frame, picks out candidate objects by thresholding and by size and shape, and keeps only the ones a trained classifier calls eggs. It shows each image with the kept objects outlined, the count drawn on it and a progress bar. When every image is done it says so, and the person downloads a CSV with one count per image.

task.text: Automatically count the eggs in every image of a batch of counting-slide images and export a table of counts, one per image.

data.text: A folder of microscope images of counting slides. The output is a table of image names and object counts.
data.item: one microscope image of a counting slide

stage.text: counting eggs in slide images after imaging, before statistical analysis of the assay

mechanism.text: A multi-file picker loads the images in the browser and sends them to the server one at a time. Each time the server finishes an image it updates a hidden signal, which tells the browser to send the next one. Meanwhile an annotated preview and a progress bar show the image just counted, and a download button exports the running table of counts.

field.text: automated egg counting from microscope images in plant nematology

workflow.name: count objects in every image of a batch and export the counts

steps.here: a multi-file picker takes a folder of .jpg, .jpeg, .png or .bmp slide images, keeps only those types and sorts them in natural name order

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: for each image it finds the counting frame, thresholds the image, keeps candidates within area and aspect-ratio limits, classifies each as egg or not egg with a neural network, and counts the eggs

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: a hidden counter changes after each image, a browser observer sees the change and sends the next file, and a progress bar shows 'Processing image i of n'
the latest image is shown scaled down, titled with its file name, with the frame drawn as a box, the eggs outlined and the count printed on it

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: after the last image a 'Processing Complete!' panel appears
'Download .csv of counts' saves counts.csv with columns image_name and count; images that failed get 'error' as their count

distinctive: Counting is a two-stage method: classical thresholding with size and shape filters proposes candidates, and a convolutional classifier decides egg or not egg.
Only objects inside the slide's counting frame are counted. The frame is found from intensity profile peaks, with fixed fallback borders when the detected size is implausible.

Only one image is in memory at a time, and the browser feeds the next file only after the server signals it is done, so a folder of any size can be processed. A keep-alive stops the session timing out.
Files over 12 MB are swapped for a blank image, and an image that fails is recorded as 'error' instead of stopping the batch.
